task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering why Orlan College's reported $40 million endowment does not function as a $40 million checking account for its projected operating-budget gap.

facts.text: Orlan College's June 2026 financial statement lists endowment assets valued at $40 million and a projected $800,000 operating-budget gap.
The endowment figure is a value of invested assets at the reporting date, not the balance of an unrestricted operating bank account.
The college's adopted annual spending plan calls for a $1.6 million endowment draw, equivalent to 4% of the stated $40 million valuation.
Of that planned draw, $1.4 million supports purposes specified in gift agreements, including scholarships and named teaching posts.
The remaining $200,000 can support general operations under the college's records.
That $200,000 is already included in the operating budget used to calculate the $800,000 gap; it is not additional new money to subtract again.
The college says changing a restricted gift's use requires a separate process and cannot be assumed from the headline asset total.
Approximately $9 million of the endowment valuation is in property and other investments that are not immediately convertible to cash at a guaranteed price.
Under the college's restricted-gift agreements, selling an asset changes the holding's form without removing the donor's specified spending limits.
Treasurer Nessa Quill says spending decisions also account for future years in which scholarships and teaching posts need support.
Quill said, "An asset can belong to the college without being available for any bill the college chooses."
Student representative Daro Linn says the distinction matters but does not answer every question about priorities within the unrestricted budget.
Linn said, "Explaining a restriction is not the same as explaining why the library is the part asked to close earlier."
The college has proposed shorter library evening hours as one possible saving but has not adopted the final operating budget.
Trustees have requested alternatives, including delayed administrative software purchases and additional unrestricted fundraising.
No new unrestricted donation has been pledged in the supplied record.
The endowment's market value can change with investment performance; the $40 million figure is not a promised future sale price.
The financial statement does not give trustees authority to spend every invested dollar immediately or establish that no other budget choice exists.
The college's oldest named scholarship dates to a 1948 gift from a former textile merchant.
Orlan enrolls 1,900 students, including commuters and residential students; the endowment is not distributed as an equal cash payment to each student.

forbidden_additions: The entire endowment is spendable cash or the unrestricted $200,000 newly reduces the stated gap to $600,000
Final library cuts, a guaranteed asset sale value or a new donation not documented
